name: Neuschwanstein
ground: A crag in the Bavarian Alps with no road, no water supply, and no strategic value of any kind, selected entirely for how it would look from below.

keep.name: The Palas
keep.note: A keep in silhouette only. There is nothing to keep.

wards.name: Upper Court
wards.note: A courtyard shaped like a bailey that never enclosed anything.

axis.name: The view from the Marienbrücke
axis.note: The whole building is composed for one viewpoint on a bridge across the gorge. Stand anywhere else and it does not resolve.

figures.value: 1869, six centuries after castles stopped working
carved, decorative, with no opening through them
11, before he died and it opened to visitors

lesson: The glossary gives you the tool to date this one at a glance: machicolations are floor openings for dropping things through, and these have no openings. They are a carving of a function. That is the whole building — a nineteenth-century theatre set quoting a form whose reasons had been dead for six hundred years, and it is the most visited castle on earth. Worth knowing which one you are building.
